dimensions.assessment: Affects individuals with traumatic brain injuries, higher-risk populations, state and tribal agencies, and public health officials.
dimensions.evidence: populations at higher risk of traumatic brain injury, including populations whose increased risk is due to occupational or circumstantial factors

dimensions.assessment: Modifies public health surveillance, data collection, and grant criteria without creating brand-new entitlements.
dimensions.evidence: Secretary, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, shall make publicly available aggregated information

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 across multiple sections of the Public Health Service Act.
Amends existing statutes relating to traumatic brain injury surveillance, state grants, and reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Section 393B of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 280b-1c) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes programs and reporting requirements running through fiscal year 2031 with permanent statutory definitions.

missing_information: Exact monetary sums for the reauthorized authorizations of appropriations were omitted in the source excerpts for certain subsections.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill reauthorizes and modifies federal traumatic brain injury programs, surveillance registries, and grant programs through fiscal year 2031, while commissioning studies and reports.
